extra.message: User-supplied 'address' field (bound from the 'ping' Struts action's request parameter) is concatenated directly into a shell command string executed via Runtime.exec({"/bin/bash","-c",...}). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; id' or '`whoami`' or '$(cmd)') in the address field to execute arbitrary OS commands with the application's privileges.

The 'name' parameter (from ProductAction.searchQuery, user-controlled via the 'listProduct' action) is concatenated directly into a JPQL query string instead of using a bound parameter. An attacker can break out of the LIKE clause to perform JPQL injection, altering query logic or extracting unintended data.

findByLoginUnsafe() concatenates the user-supplied 'login' parameter directly into a JPQL query string ('WHERE u.login = ''' + login + ''''), unlike the parameterized findByLogin() elsewhere in the same class. It is invoked from UserAction.search() (the authenticated 'userSearch' action), allowing JPQL injection via the login field (e.g. closing the quote to alter the WHERE clause).

adminShowUsers() (exposed unauthenticated at /api/userList — the 'api' package in struts.xml has no authenticationStack interceptor) grants admin access and dumps every user's id/login/email/role solely based on a client-supplied cookie named 'admin' equal to '1' (lines 39-44). Cookies are fully attacker-controlled; anyone can send 'Cookie: admin=1' to bypass authentication entirely and exfiltrate all user accounts. The application's actual role model (User.isAdmin()/role field) is never consulted here.

The password-reset 'key' is required to equal MD5(login) with no server-side secret, salt, or expiry (DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex(login.getBytes())). Anyone who knows or guesses a user's login can compute this value offline and reset that user's password via the unauthenticated 'resetPasswordExecute' action, fully bypassing authentication.

The 'url' field is fully user-controlled (set via request parameter) and any non-empty value triggers the 'redirect' result. struts.xml wires this to '<result name="redirect" type="redirect">${url}</result>' (struts.xml:101), sending the HTTP redirect Location header to the raw user-supplied URL with no allow-list or same-origin validation, enabling phishing/open-redirect attacks.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: execute() creates/updates arbitrary products (entityManager.persist/merge via productService.save) for any session that merely passes the generic authenticationStack (login-only) interceptor — there is no check against User.isAdmin()/role, even though that role model exists elsewhere in the codebase (User.java:88-90). Any authenticated, non-privileged user can create or modify the entire product catalog.

ping() is exposed at /api/ping with no interceptor (no authenticationStack in the 'api' package of struts.xml), and for any 'login' value looks the user up and returns their email address in the JSON response. This lets an unauthenticated attacker enumerate valid logins and harvest associated email addresses. It also throws an unhandled NullPointerException (user.getEmail() on a null 'user') when the login does not exist, since findByLogin() can return null but is not checked before use.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: resetPasswordByLogin() logs the user's new plaintext password to the application log via logger.info("... New password: " + password), persisting sensitive credential material in log files where it can be read by anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
